codes.justification: The clause allocates indemnification responsibility between the Owner and Contractor for claims arising from negligence or breach of contract, establishing risk allocation and management of liability between the parties.
The clause governs payment of portions of the Profit Pool at determined milestones, addressing timing and amounts of payment under the Contract.
The clause addresses payment for samples required for tests or inspections designated in the Contract Documents, directly relating to inspection procedures.
The clause allocates the cost obligation for samples related to testing/inspection to the Trade Contractor.
The clause allocates and waives claims/liability risk between the Design-Builder and Owner arising from Work or Design Services, establishing which risks are retained or released.
The clause governs claims, notice requirements, and preservation of rights to claims, which relates to the process for asserting and preserving matters in question between the parties.
This clause is part of the claims process for a change in Contract Price, establishing the Construction Manager's obligation to issue findings on a claim within a set timeframe.
The clause establishes a procedural step (findings by the Construction Manager) that forms part of the process for resolving a matter in question between the parties regarding a claim.
This clause allocates and caps liability between the parties, establishing limits on risk exposure under the Contract, a core risk allocation mechanism.
The clause ties liability limits to the amount of applicable insurance required under GC 11.1 – INSURANCE, directly referencing insurance coverage requirements.
The clause addresses the Payment Certifier's role in relation to the Design-Builder's applications for payment, referencing progress payment provisions.
The clause addresses the rejection of a payment application and requires notice in compliance with Payment Legislation, directly relating to final payment procedures.

The clause requires the Owner to provide timely information and approvals necessary for the orderly progress of the Pre-construction Services, Construction Services, and the Work, establishing a broad obligation supporting execution of the Work.
Clause addresses entitlement to Profit Pool payment for Design Services and Work completed at termination, net of deductions, which is a payment mechanics provision.
The clause allocates responsibility for loss and damage incurred due to default and ties it to set-off/deduction rights, an allocation of risk between parties upon termination.
The clause allocates and limits indemnification obligations between the parties, capping liability for various loss categories, which is a form of risk allocation and management.
The clause ties indemnification limits directly to insurance coverage required under GC 11.1, referencing insurance limits for losses covered or not covered by insurance.

The clause governs the process for submitting a claim for adjustment in Contract Price, GMP, or Target Contract Price, requiring a detailed account of the amount claimed and grounds, which is part of the change/claim procedure under the Contract.
This clause establishes the order of priority and consistency rules among Contract Documents, drawings, and specifications, ensuring coordination and resolving conflicts between design documents.
This clause establishes the warranty period during which defects in the Work may be identified and remedied, directly tied to correction of non-conforming Work obligations.
The clause addresses how the Contract Price accounts for overhead and profit in relation to cash allowances, which pertains to payment mechanics and pricing treatment.
The clause requires submission of Construction Documents for Owner review to ensure consistency with the Contract Documents and coordination between the parties.
The clause requires submission 'in orderly sequence' and a jointly prepared schedule for submission and return of documents, addressing timing and sequencing of these submissions.
The clause concerns the designation and continuity of the Payment Certifier, a role central to certification of payment under the Contract.
The clause governs timing and consolidation of arbitration proceedings, part of the negotiation, mediation and arbitration process for resolving disputes.
Provides for the Design-Builder to be paid for Design Services performed and other damages including profit upon deemed termination.
The clause identifies default triggers tied to payment certification and payment of certified amounts, including failure to issue certificates under GC 5.3 or pay amounts due.
The clause allocates the risk of Owner default and establishes conditions under which the Design-Builder may act, addressing management of contractual risk between the parties.
The clause conditions Owner occupancy on regulatory approval, managing risk associated with early occupancy prior to authority sign-off.
The clause governs the timing and dating of applications for progress payment, a core payment application mechanic.
The clause requires establishing a date for finishing remaining Work following Ready-for-Takeover, addressing timing/scheduling of the Work's completion.
The clause allocates responsibility for correcting default and establishes the compliance standard for remedying a breach, managing risk of continued default.
Clause allocates indemnification responsibility between Owner and Design-Builder for claims arising from toxic/hazardous substance obligations, an allocation of contractual risk.
The indemnity relates specifically to obligations under GC 9.2 concerning toxic and hazardous substances and materials, an environmental matter.
Clause addresses discovery of toxic or hazardous substances at the Place of the Work and requires action to limit exposure, directly implicating environmental/hazardous substance obligations.
The clause allocates responsibility to the Construction Manager to take reasonable steps and report, managing risk arising from undisclosed hazardous conditions.
Shop Drawings are submittals that ensure the Work's details are coordinated with and consistent with the design intent in the Contract Documents.
Requiring the Contractor to provide Shop Drawings as required in the Contract Documents establishes a duty governing performance of the Work.

The clause establishes the Design-Builder's responsibility for Design Services performed by the Consultant and Other Consultants, addressing the standard of care and consistency expected in delivering those design services under the Contract.
The clause allocates responsibility to the Design-Builder for ensuring Design Services meet a professional standard of care, effectively assigning risk for design performance to the Design-Builder.
The clause allocates responsibility between Owner and Construction Manager for obtaining and paying for permits, approvals, and easements, establishing a division of regulatory risk/responsibility.
The clause addresses intellectual property rights (patent, copyright, trademark) in Instruments of Service, which relates to ownership rights in Contract Documents/deliverables.
This clause preserves statutory termination rights under the Civil Code of Québec, addressing allocation of contractual risk regarding termination rights not being waived by the contract.
This clause states the total amount payable by the Owner to the Design-Builder, directly establishing the Contract Price payment amount.

This clause establishes the arbitration referral process following mediated negotiations, specifying notice requirements, timing, and the applicable arbitration rules and jurisdiction, directly implementing the dispute resolution mechanism.
The clause addresses how cash discounts accrue in relation to payment funds deposited by the Owner, which is part of the payment mechanics under the Cost of the Work provisions.

The clause establishes supervision duties requiring the Construction Manager to provide supervision and maintain a competent representative at the Place of the Work, which governs how the Work is performed and overseen under the Contract.
The clause expressly establishes that physical models furnished at the Owner's expense become the property of the Owner, addressing ownership/title.

This clause is part of the Waiver of Claims provisions and requires submission of a detailed account of the amount claimed following a Notice in Writing of claim, forming part of the claims/dispute process under the Contract.

The clause addresses toxic and hazardous substances at the Place of the Work, an environmental/hazardous materials matter, and allocates deemed control and management to the Owner regarding existing conditions.
